subject.title: fix(agents): bound stalled SSH directory uploads with an idle watchdog

question: Should sandbox uploads be permitted to remain locally quiet after `tar` has finished while SSH completes its remaining handshake, remote-command, or buffered-transfer work, rather than treating that state as a stalled upload?
rationale: The PR changes an existing no-deadline behavior for all callers, but the available local progress signal cannot reliably tell a dead connection from valid post-producer SSH work; choosing the permanent compatibility boundary requires owner intent.

options.title: Require an SSH-aware liveness boundary
options.body: Revise the guard so it cannot kill a valid upload solely because the local tar producer has finished, and add the delayed-small-upload regression test.

options.title: Accept the 30-second producer-idle limit
options.body: Merge the current behavior as an intentional compatibility change that may fail very slow valid post-producer SSH work.

options.title: Pause this change
options.body: Keep the existing behavior until the sandbox owner chooses a reliable observable boundary for the reported handshake stall.

recommendation.title: Require an SSH-aware liveness boundary
recommendation.body: Revise the guard so it cannot kill a valid upload solely because the local tar producer has finished, and add the delayed-small-upload regression test.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR author has the most direct evidence on the proposed timeout semantics and can incorporate the selected boundary, although current-main area ownership remains unconfirmed.
